title: Ministries
tomorrow: why did Jesus stand up to read, then sit down to talk?

cards: Count the people up front at a Sunday Mass who aren't the priest: someone reading, servers in robes, a choir, people holding the cups at Communion. Where did they all come from? The answer starts with a complaint.
In the Acts of the Apostles, the young church in Jerusalem is growing fast, and food is handed out daily to widows. Then the Greek-speaking believers begin to murmur: our widows are being overlooked.
The apostles are stretched thin. So they call the whole community together, and they say…

teach.h: WE CAN'T LEAVE THE WORD TO SERVE TABLES.
teach.b: …it isn't right for us to leave the word of God and serve tables.
Choose from among you seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and wisdom, and we'll put them over this work. The whole crowd likes the plan.
They choose Stephen and six others, and the apostles pray and lay hands on them. Tradition sees in these seven the first deacons.
Notice how ministry is born here: from a need someone noticed, and from people willing to say, I can do that.

Paul gives it a picture in his first letter to the Corinthians, one body with many members: "Now there are diversities of graces, but the same Spirit." The eye can't say to the hand, I don't need you.
That's the room on Sunday. Readers who lend their voice, servers at the altar, a choir, ministers of Communion, visitors who carry Communion to the sick, catechists who teach.
One to tell a friend: the Second Vatican Council taught that lay people share in Christ's mission through their baptism, not through a job title.
On that teaching, everyone serves. A ministry just gives the serving a shape.

how: Parishes have lay readers (lectors), altar servers, choirs, extraordinary ministers of Holy Communion, visitors to the sick and catechists, alongside the priest and deacon.

o: the shapes service takes in a parish community
the government offices that run a country

p: we can't leave the word to serve tables

s: in Acts, the apostles picked the seven without asking anyone
they called the whole community together, and the crowd chose them.

games.q: you're one of the apostles. the Greek-speaking widows are being missed at the daily meal, and you're stretched thin. what do you do?
o: call everyone together and have them choose people to serve.
work longer hours and serve all the tables yourselves.
tell the widows to wait until things calm down.
games.why: the apostles gathered the community, which chose seven, and they prayed and laid hands on them. a ministry was born from a need.

practice: Take a pen and paper and write one thing you're good at, plainly, the way you'd tell a friend: I can cook, I can fix bikes, I'm good with little kids, I can carry a tune.
Under it, write one place it could serve, in a parish or anywhere people gather. If you pray, you can offer that line to God just as it is.

wordCard.voice: Ministries. The shapes that service takes in a parish, each one born from a need and a person willing to meet it. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: service, ministry. the word for the daily serving of the widows in Acts 6:1.

carryVoice: Carry this: everyone serves, from the first seven at the tables to whoever reads on Sunday. See you tomorrow.
